title: Speak, Lord (1 Samuel 3)
hookLine: a boy wakes three times to a voice and learns to say speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth

lines: THE WORD OF THE LORD WAS RARE.
HERE I AM. YOU CALLED ME.
cards: It's the middle of the night in the sanctuary at Shiloh. The lamp of God hasn't gone out yet. An old priest, Eli, is asleep in his place; his eyes have grown so dim he can barely see.
A boy is asleep near the ark of God: Samuel, Hannah's son, the one she gave to the Lord. The text adds a sad note about those days: the word of the Lord was rare, and visions were few.
Then, in the dark, someone calls the boy's name. Samuel runs to the old man. Here I am.
You called me. Eli rolls over: I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.

teach.h: THREE TIMES TO THE WRONG ROOM.
teach.b: It happens again, and then a third time. And the text gives the reason he keeps getting it wrong: "Samuel did not yet know the Lord."
He's grown up in the house of God, serves there every day, and doesn't recognize God's voice. That isn't a failure. He's simply young.
On the third time, the old man understands. Eli, who has his own failings, and whose sons have been a disgrace, still knows this much: it's God. So he gives the boy one line to say.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth."

teach.h: SAMUEL DID NOT YET KNOW THE LORD.
teach.b: Samuel lies down again, and the text says the Lord came and stood, and called as before: Samuel, Samuel. This time the boy says it.

teach.h: THE OLD PRIEST GIVES HIM A LINE.
teach.b: Notice what the line does. Speak comes first: Samuel asks for the word. Then heareth: he promises to listen.
In Hebrew, heareth is the same verb as the Shema's hear, the hear, O Israel this path met not long ago.

teach.h: A HARD MESSAGE IN THE MORNING.
teach.b: And what God says is hard: judgment on Eli's house. In the morning Samuel is afraid to tell him. Eli insists, and Samuel tells him everything.
Hearing God can mean carrying a message you'd rather not. The Church reads this chapter at Sunday Mass beside the call of Jesus's first disciples in John's Gospel.

teach.h: SPEAK, LORD, FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.
teach.b: And some Catholics pray speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth as a whole prayer, with no other words.

how: Some Catholics use Samuel's words, speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth, as a short prayer before reading scripture or in quiet adoration, and the chapter is read on a Sunday in Ordinary Time alongside the call of the first disciples.

s: Samuel recognized God's voice the first time
he ran to Eli three times. the text says he did not yet know the Lord.

God's first message to Samuel was good news for Eli

games.q: you're Samuel. God has just told you that Eli's house will be judged. in the morning, Eli asks what you heard. what do you do?
o: tell him everything, and hide nothing.
soften it so he won't be hurt.
say you must have been dreaming.
games.why: Samuel tells him all of it. Eli answers, it is the Lord: let him do what is good in his sight. hearing God can mean carrying a hard word.

practice: If you pray, say Samuel's line once, slowly, speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth, then stop talking and listen, the way you'd listen in a dark room for someone calling your name.
If you don't pray, simply listen: to the room, your breath, whatever has been trying to get your attention. Nothing may come, and that's all right; Samuel ran to the wrong room three times.

wordCard.voice: Speak. The first word of Samuel's answer in the night, and the start of a whole prayer: speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: hearing, listening, the root of the Shema. Samuel's line ends with it: thy servant is listening.

carryVoice: Your line: thy servant heareth. Three wrong rooms, and then the right answer. Until tomorrow.
